findings.summary: The empty-bullet override fires for any lone `-` line following a paragraph anywhere in the document, not just inside an existing list item, breaking legitimate single-dash setext headings at the top level.
findings.evidence:
isEmptyBulletLine(state, line) only checks that the current line's indentation is >= state.blkIndent and that it is a bare `-`/`*`/`+` marker followed by whitespace only — it never checks that the paragraph above is actually nested under an existing list item. Combined with wrappedList's guard `silent && state.parentType === 'paragraph' && isEmptyBulletLine(...)` (lines 180-190) and the isLoneDash change in lheadingRule (lines ~104-118), this fires identically for top-level text like: ``` My Title - ``` Tracing the code: lheadingRule sets state.parentType='paragraph' while probing ahead (line 77), evaluates the underline candidate on line "-", sees marker===DASH with runLength===1 so isLoneDash=true, skips the 'level=...; break' path, and (regardless of outcome) lheadingRule returns false because level stays 0 (no heading built). Then the plain 'paragraph' rule runs for "My Title", itself scanning ahead via terminatorRules (which include wrappedList) with parentType='paragraph'; wrappedList sees isEmptyBulletLine(state, nextLine) is true for the lone "-" line (blkIndent is 0 at top level, so the check trivially passes) and returns true, terminating the paragraph before the "-" line. The main tokenizer then re-parses "-" from scratch (silent=false), where wrappedList delegates to the stock list rule, which is now free to start a brand-new top-level list (since it is no longer 'interrupting' a paragraph — the paragraph already ended). Net result: `My Title\n-` renders as `

My Title

` instead of the correct/previous `

My Title

`, for any single-dash setext heading anywhere in a note, not only the intended '- 1\n -' nested-bullet case described in the plugin's own doc comment ("a lone empty bullet under a list item"). The added tests only cover the multi-dash ('---') setext case (preview.test.ts, 'preserves multi-dash setext headings'), so this single-dash regression is untested and would ship silently.

verdict.reason:
Traced the code and it matches the reviewer's description. isEmptyBulletLine (list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:31-49) only checks state.sCount[line] >= state.blkIndent (trivially true at top level where blkIndent=0) and the bare marker shape; it never checks that the line is nested inside an existing list item. wrappedList's guard (lines 181-193) fires whenever silent && state.parentType === 'paragraph' && isEmptyBulletLine(...), and state.parentType is set to 'paragraph' by both the modified lheadingRule (line 77) and the stock paragraph rule while probing terminator candidates, regardless of nesting depth. lheadingRule's isLoneDash check (lines 96-113) unconditionally suppresses the setext-heading outcome for any single-dash line and falls through to the terminator-rule loop (118-126) where wrappedList reports termination, so the paragraph stops before the '-' line; the tokenizer then re-parses '-' non-silently with parentType reset, letting the stock list rule open a brand-new list without CommonMark's 'empty item cannot interrupt a paragraph' restriction. This reproduces 'My Title\n-' -> '

My Title

' instead of '

My Title

' for any top-level lone-dash line, not just the nested '- 1\n -' case the plugin's own doc comment and issue #517 describe. preview.test.ts (151-195) only tests the nested case and the multi-dash top-level setext case; there is no test for a bare top-level single-dash setext heading, so this path is unverified. The design doc (docs/design/notes/notes.md:276-299) and the plugin's own JSDoc frame the intended fix around an empty bullet nested under a list item, but the implementation enforces no such scoping check, so the broader top-level breakage appears to be a real, unguarded side effect rather than a deliberately scoped and verified behavior.
